# workspace-memory

Long-term notes and full-text recall for workspace mode.

- **Runs in:** the harness process
- **Source:** [lisp/modules/harness-workspace-memory.el](../../lisp/modules/harness-workspace-memory.el)
- **Loaded:** when enabled (see `harness-enable-modules`)
- **Requires:** [store](store.md), [session](session.md), [tools](tools.md)
- **Required by:** [workspace](workspace.md)

## About

The workspace's memory is a small, durable note store with a full-text
index.  Every user and assistant message of a workspace episode is
written here as a note, and `memory/search` is what the
workspace's brief asks for the thread it is about to continue.

This is the local half of the design's memory layer.  It is
deliberately a cache of the distilled conversation, not a second
transcript index: the notes are short, they carry the workspace and
the thread, and they are searched by the same words a person would
use.  A Logseq backend can replace the store behind the same four
methods without changing the workspace or the UI.

Storage is SQLite in the harness state directory, with FTS5 when the
build has it and a LIKE fallback when it does not.  The database is a
cache: rebuilding it is a matter of reading the notes again from the
timeline, which this module can do with `workspace-memory/rebuild`.

## Provides

### Methods

- `memory/forget` (workspace id &optional opts) — Delete note ID of WORKSPACE and return what was removed.
- `memory/get` (workspace id &optional opts) — Return note ID of WORKSPACE, or signal when it is not there.
- `memory/notes` (workspace &optional opts) — Return the notes of WORKSPACE, newest first.
- `memory/page` (workspace page &optional opts) — Return the note page of WORKSPACE's PAGE, newest first.
- `memory/pages` (workspace &optional filter) — Return the pages of WORKSPACE, one per thread with its note count.
- `memory/recall-test` (workspace query) — Return what a brief would recall for QUERY in WORKSPACE.
- `memory/reindex` (workspace &optional opts) — Rebuild the full-text index of WORKSPACE and return its counts.
- `memory/remember` (session-id text &optional thread) — Write TEXT as a note for SESSION-ID's workspace and THREAD.
- `memory/search` (workspace query &optional opts) — Return notes of WORKSPACE that match QUERY, best first.
- `memory/status` (&optional workspace) — Return what the memory holds for WORKSPACE, or for every workspace.
- `memory/sync` (workspace &optional opts) — Bring the index of WORKSPACE up to date and return its counts.
- `memory/write` (workspace thread role text &optional opts) — Write TEXT as a note of WORKSPACE's THREAD.

### Tools

- `memory_search` — Search the workspace's long-term notes. Use it for anything the brief did not give you, for a decision from another thread, or for a preference the user mentioned before. Returns the matching notes with their thread and role; never invent a memory you did not retrieve.
- `memory_status` — Say how many notes the workspace memory holds and when the last one was written.
- `memory_write` — Write a durable memory note for the workspace: a preference, a decision, a commitment, a fact about a person or project, or an open loop. Use it when the user asks you to remember, when a decision is made, or when a commitment is created. It is not a transcript dump.

### Options

- `harness-workspace-memory-default-limit` — Notes a search returns by default.
- `harness-workspace-memory-max-chars` — Most characters of one note the memory keeps.
